newsitem.title: JAPAN: Comson shares ask-only after failing to honor note.
newsitem.headline: Comson shares ask-only after failing to honor note.

text.p: Shares in Japanese machinery maker Comson Corp were ask-only on the Osaka Securities Exchange on Wednesday after announcement on Tuesday that it had failed to honour promissory notes for the first time, brokers said.
As of 0026 GMT, the shares were ask only at 160 yen, compared with its Tuesday close of 165 yen.
After the stock market closed on Tuesday, the company announced that it had failed to honour promissory notes totalling 150 million yen due on June 30.
A Japanese firm which fails to honour promissory notes for a second time is considered insolvent.
Comson president Toshimi Matsuda told a news conference in Osaka on Tuesday that the company would strive to improve management in order to avoid such failures in the future.
The company is due to pay 30 million yen worth of promissory notes on July 20 and about 300 million yen worth at the end of July.

Matsuda also said that there was no change in its plan to issue up to $10 million worth of convertible bonds. The company has been in talks with underwriters over its planned issue of $8 million worth of convertible bonds in July, he said.
